A product search component keeps its

before the assertion, the test passes, and the team notes that "signals are async". They aren't:

It looks like the right tool because it reads like a watcher, and watchers are how many of us learned reactivity: a

even refused signal writes unless you passed

as stale. The next read of

An effect works the other way. Writing to a signal it reads only marks it dirty, and Angular runs it later: a component's effects run during change detection, just before that component is checked. Until then,
holds the previous list. Any code that writes

in the same synchronous block, like a handler that opens the only result when Enter is pressed, or a unit test, sees stale data. When the effect finally runs, its write lands in the middle of change detection, so Angular has more to check. The docs list the costs of propagating state this way: NG0100 errors (
), infinite circular updates, and unnecessary change detection cycles.
